blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Re-reviewed 2026-10-19. asUSDF is a direct non-proxy token on BSC (0x917af46b3c3c6e1bb7286b9f59637fb7c65851fb; EIP-1967 implementation slot zero) holding 100% of supply. Verified source exposes ADMIN_ROLE pause()/unpause() over ERC20Pausable and MINTER_AND_BURN_ROLE mint(address,uint256)/burn(address,uint256). At BSC block 128505031, paused() returned false; ADMIN_ROLE was held by 4-of-7 Safe 0xa8c0c6ee62f5ad95730fe23ccf37d1c1ffaa1c3f and MINTER_AND_BURN_ROLE by the asUSDFEarn minting contract 0xdB57a53C428a9faFcbFefFB6dd80d0f427543695. Verified asUSDFEarn source calls asUSDF.burn(address(this), amount) on withdrawal, so the role member cannot destroy another holder's balance. DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE is held by 6-hour Timelock 0xe829a87f4dfa41b032d8b6feca6c2213d6ee1861, which can grant the role to a new burner. Global pause plus an admin-grantable burner is a mutable holder-facing surface but not an active holder-selective control, so the status is Possible. Upstream USDF exposure is additional but does not change a direct Possible.

oracleRisk.summary: asUSDF is a NAV-accreting staking wrapper minted from deposited USDF and withdrawn back to USDF through Aster's queue, not a borrower debt market with oracle-triggered collateral liquidation.

branchApplicability.rationale: Aster documents asUSDF as a yield-bearing wrapper whose APY is reflected in its net asset value. Staking mints shares and withdrawal converts those shares back to USDF through a queue; there are no borrower-specific collateral or liquidation branches, but the wrapper NAV is a price-sensitive top-level redemption and valuation authority.
